s: threatens State [when she came] The winged songstress came to the State and was tested and tried before everyone. Oedipus is credited with saving the State in connection with her appearance.

l: oracle’s voice, Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
s: A divine voice from Earth’s mid shrine summons a search near and far for the undiscovered murderer.

l: Merope, Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
s: Merope is identified by Oedipus as his mother and as a Dorian.

l: the surviving herdsman, Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
s: The surviving herdsman is Laius’s serf, household thrall, and shepherd. Sole survivor of Laius’s death, he returns to Thebes and reports the murder. Sent to mountain pastures by Jocasta, he receives her infant Oedipus to be destroyed because of a prophecy, but pities and spares him, giving him to the Corinthian Messenger. Oedipus later orders him brought back for questioning.

l: the crossroads, Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
s: is_located_in Phocis [where the roads from Delphi and Daulis meet] The crossroads, where branches from Delphi and Daulis meet, is identified as the place where Laius was reportedly murdered. Oedipus recalls encountering and killing an older man and his attendants at a place with three branching roads.

l: the oracle concerning Laius, Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
s: foretells Laius's murder [by Laius’s own son] The oracle concerning Laius declared that Laius would perish by the hand of his own son. Jocasta says Laius’s infant son was exposed and that the prophecy did not come true because the child supposedly died before killing him.

l: the quarrel between Oedipus and Creon, Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
s: The quarrel between Oedipus and Creon begins when Oedipus accuses Creon of arranging the seer’s charge and plotting to take the crown. Jocasta and the Chorus intervene, after which Oedipus allows Creon to leave despite continuing to hate and suspect him.

l: Antigone’s family curse, Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
s: Antigone’s family curse is a persistent affliction of the Labdacidae, centered on Oedipus. After recognizing that he may have killed Laius, Oedipus sees himself as cursed through birth, marriage, and parricide; his established guilt requires exile, while Jocasta seeks cleansing for the land.

l: Oedipus's alleged crimes, Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
s: include Laius's murder [as alleged by the seer] Oedipus’s alleged crimes are killing Laius, defiling the bed of the man he killed, marrying his own mother, and killing his father. He fears that the first of these may already have occurred and that the rest may follow the prophecy.

l: Corinthian Messenger, Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
s: A messenger from Corinth who tends mountain flocks, finds the abandoned infant Oedipus in Cithaeron, and gives him to Polybus. Later he reports Polybus’s death and Corinth’s choice of Oedipus as king, revealing Oedipus’s adoption.

l: oracle, Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
s: Oracle foretells Oedipus killing his father and marrying his mother; seemingly disproved by Polybus’s death, its prophecy is later revealed fulfilled.

l: death of Polybus, Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
s: is_a death [natural death after a full lifespan] The Corinthian Messenger announces that Polybus has died naturally after living through the full span of his years. His death initially reassures Jocasta and Oedipus, but it is later shown not to disprove the prophecy because Polybus was not Oedipus’s biological father.

l: Oedipus’s birth revelation, Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
s: The Corinthian Messenger and Laius’s Herdsman reveal that Oedipus was born to Laius and Jocasta, exposed as an infant, and given to the Messenger. Oedipus learns that Polybus and Merope were not his biological parents.

l: parricide, Plays of Sophocles: Oedipus the King; Oedipus at Colonus; Antigone
s: Oedipus had feared that he would kill his father, but he believed Polybus’s death without his involvement disproved the prediction. After learning that Laius was his biological father, he recognizes that his killing of Laius was the foretold parricide.
